Hydration advice is full of myths that have hung around far longer than the evidence behind them, and a few are worth clearing up.

## The eight-glasses rule

The idea that everyone needs exactly eight glasses of water a day isn't well supported — actual needs vary with body size, activity level, and climate.

## Thirst is a reliable signal

For most healthy people, thirst is actually a fairly reliable guide to hydration needs, and forcing extra water beyond that doesn't provide much additional benefit.

## Other drinks count too

Coffee, tea, and water-rich foods all contribute to daily fluid intake, despite the persistent myth that only plain water "counts."

Paying attention to your own body's signals, rather than chasing a fixed number of glasses, is generally a better strategy than following a one-size-fits-all hydration rule.
